title: RWB-S9-E6029-APP: the onboarding write has no published operation, partner_user has no field list, the terms have no linking column, and the reference-data read has no plan row
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6029-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12); legacy RWB-E6-029; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A1.3, A1.4, A2.1 and A2.2; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.1, T6.1, T6.2, T7 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-26, R-UNI-28 and R-UNI-29; Event and Messaging Design v4, EV-20 and EV-21
description: (1) The panel write that FEAT-PRM-01 needs is in no inventory: TSD S9 T-A.1 lists API-S9-001 GET /partners and the five instruction operations only, and the ownership rows give six operations, none of them a create or update of a partner, so the method, the path, the request element and its right carry the placeholder. (2) S9's ownership rows give three tables, partner, partner_instruction and partner_user, while TSD S9 T3.1 publishes field definitions for partner and partner_instruction only, so partner_user has no field list and no BR Field ID. (3) No field links a partner to the version of a fee schedule, a service level or a scope, so the terms FEAT-PRM-01 names are reference data of FEAT-PRM-02 with no recorded link to the partner. (4) DP-07 is absent from the pattern set although the two lists are reference data of rwb-case by default ruling, the plan's C row is None, and no operation name is published for the read. (5) DP-06 and DP-08 are absent although the TSD names parameters, reference data and a role and permission matrix as reused capabilities. (6) DP-09 is absent although the service owns topic rwb.partner.events.v1 with EV-20 and consumes EV-21. (7) No message ID is published for the 409 of a duplicate partner_code, and TSD S9 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes with no message ID per condition. (8) The legacy feature dependency FEAT-OCC-13 is named by the FSD as a prerequisite and its owning service is named by no S9 source. (9) The plan carries no requirement id for this slice while TSD S9 T8 gives REQ-S9-001 to REQ-S9-004 and REQ-S9-008 to FEAT-PRM-01. (10) The partner gateway that fronts this service on FAPI 2.0 is an edge capability that no pattern row and no dependency row carries.
evidence: TSD S9 T-A.1 (six operations, none of them a partner create); context pack ownership rows (tables 3, REST operations provided 6, events 2, jobs 0, workflows 1); TSD S9 T3.1 (partner and partner_instruction only); TSD S9 T3.2 (LOV-PANEL, LOV-PARTNER-TYPE); FSD S9 A2.1.2 prerequisites (FEAT-OCC-13); split plan slice RWB-S9-E6029-APP (H three rows, C and X empty, reqs empty); Architecture v5 slide 8 (partner gateway FAPI 2.0 to S9)
area: Contract surface, data model, dependencies and messages
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-partner tech lead, the rwb-case reference-data owner and the API owner
proposed: Publish the onboarding write in the rwb-partner contract with the created and updated partner as one shape under /api/recovery/partner/v1, right C; add partner_user to the TSD field catalogue with its BR Field IDs; add the plan rows for the reference-data read as C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and for the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; carry the partner gateway as an edge dependency of the service and bind the 409 to a message ID; keep the terms with FEAT-PRM-02 and record whether a partner-to-version link is needed at all.

title: RWB-S9-E6029-CON: the onboarding operation, the partner_user shape, the terms link, the consumed operation name and the conflict message have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E6029-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner; legacy RWB-E6-029; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.1.2, A2.1.3, A2.1.4.3 and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v2 T2, T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.1, T6.1, T6.2, T7 and T-A.1 and T-A.2; API Specification v4, Partner; NFR-050
description: (1) No source publishes the method, the path or the request element of the onboarding write, so the baseline declares the created and updated partner as one shape with the placeholder and no new endpoint name. (2) The ownership rows give six operations and the TSD inventory lists six, but the panel write is in neither, so API-S9-001 is the only operation the baseline can declare from a source and the second carries the placeholder. (3) partner_user is a table of S9 with no field list in TSD S9 T3.1, so the baseline names the portal scope of NFR-050 and leaves the shape to the DB story. (4) No property or table links a partner to the version of a fee schedule, a service level or a scope, so the baseline declares no such property. (5) The reference-data read of the two lists carries no operation name in any source and the plan's C row is None. (6) TSD S9 T-A.2 gives error sets as status codes with no message ID per condition and publishes no required list for the request, so the required list of the answer is taken from the TSD required column and each condition is bound to a message of the legacy and FSD set. (7) No message ID exists for the 409 of a duplicate partner_code. (8) EV-20 and EV-21 are published in no catalogue under their target names, only the naming rule of Template and Rules R4 gives the form.
evidence: TSD S9 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (operation inventory and endpoint detail, no partner create, error sets as status codes); TSD S9 T3.1 (no partner_user); context pack ownership rows (REST operations provided 6, tables 3); FSD S9 A2.1.3 (field catalog) and A2.1.4.3 (two exception flows); TSD S9 T7 NFR-050 (partner account scope); split plan slice RWB-S9-E6029-CON (H, C, I and X empty)
area: Contract surface, data shape, consumed rows and messages
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-partner tech lead and the rwb-case reference-data owner
proposed: Baseline the onboarding write with its method, path and request element, or confirm that the panel read and the write are one operation; publish partner_user in the TSD field catalogue; name the reference-data operation and add RWB-P3-E1043-CON to the C row; bind the 409 to a message ID; publish the target event names of EV-20 and EV-21 in the event catalogue.
